Thanks Emily — that’s super helpful. Looping in Laura (legal/ops) and Dev (SE) to get the right docs ready before the procurement call.

Below is a concise view of procurement/commercial paths and how they map to technical packaging — this should help procurement pick the right path:

1) Hosted (Redwood API, on-demand):
   - Procurement: easiest (card or invoice), fastest time-to-production.
   - Billing: monthly, usage-based.
   - When to pick: early POC, variable volume, minimal ops overhead.

2) Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity):
   - Procurement: typically requires a contract + statement of work; supports PO.
   - Billing: committed monthly/annual spend (can be invoiced via PO). Commits reduce per-token costs substantially.
   - When to pick: predictable high-throughput workloads and need for cost predictability / isolation.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem):
   - Procurement: enterprise contract + longer procurement cycle; usually SOW + infra onboarding.
   - Billing: platform fee + support; commits common.
   - When to pick: regulated data, strict network controls, or on-prem requirements.

Marketplace vs Direct SOW: marketplace purchases can speed procurement approvals (Procurement likes one-click marketplace billing) but sometimes limit contract flexibility (legal redlines). If you want the shortest procurement path, marketplace is often faster; if you need custom SLA/KMS terms, direct SOW is better.

Commit vs On-demand: a 12–24 month committed plan (Dedicated) gives ~30–45% unit-cost reduction vs Hosted on-demand; we’ll attach two estimate scenarios in the pricing sheet (on-demand, 12-mo commit, 24-mo commit).

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Share SOW template + updated pricing matrix (attached).
- Draft an initial Dedicated 12-mo and Hosted burst estimate for your forecasted volume and send by EOD.
- Schedule a procurement + legal alignment call for Tue 10am PT (tentative) — please confirm.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_template.pdf, pricing_summary_v2.xlsx

Thanks —
Aditya
